CARDIAC_ARREST.title: CPR / Suspected Cardiac Arrest
CARDIAC_ARREST.disclaimer: VERIFY AGAINST AHA / RED CROSS GUIDELINES. Operator must confirm unconsciousness and absence of normal breathing before advising chest compressions.
steps: Ensure the scene is safe for the caller and patient.
Check responsiveness: Shake shoulders gently and shout 'Are you okay?'
Check breathing: Look at chest for 5 to 10 seconds. If not breathing or only gasping, start CPR.
Place patient flat on their back on a firm, flat surface.
Place the heel of one hand on the center of the chest (lower half of breastbone). Place other hand on top, interlocking fingers.
Push hard and fast: 100 to 120 compressions per minute (to the beat of 'Stayin' Alive'). Allow full chest recoil.
Compress to a depth of at least 2 inches (5 cm). Do not stop until paramedics arrive or an AED is ready.
CARDIAC_ARREST.voice_prompt: Place the person flat on their back. Put both hands in the center of their chest. Push down hard and fast, two times every second, until the ambulance arrives.

SEVERE_BLEEDING.title: Severe Bleeding & Hemorrhage Control
SEVERE_BLEEDING.disclaimer: VERIFY AGAINST RED CROSS FIRST AID PROTOCOLS. Do not remove objects deeply embedded in the wound.
steps: Ensure immediate scene safety and protect yourself from blood exposure if possible.
Apply direct, firm pressure on the wound using a clean cloth, sterile gauze, or hands.
Do not remove soaked dressings; apply additional cloths directly over existing ones.
If bleeding is from an arm or leg and does not stop with direct pressure, apply an emergency tourniquet 2-3 inches above the wound (not over a joint).
Keep the patient lying down, warm, and calm to prevent hemorrhagic shock.
SEVERE_BLEEDING.voice_prompt: Take a clean cloth or towel. Press down directly on the wound with both hands. Keep pressing firmly. Do not lift the cloth to check.

FIRE_AND_BURNS.title: Fire Emergency & Thermal Burn Protocol
FIRE_AND_BURNS.disclaimer: VERIFY AGAINST NATIONAL FIRE PROTECTION ASSOCIATION & RED CROSS FIRST AID. Immediate evacuation takes absolute priority over first aid.
steps: EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY: Get everyone out of the building. Do not use elevators.
If smoke is present, stay low to the floor where air is cleaner. Cover mouth and nose with a damp cloth if available.
If clothes catch fire: STOP, DROP, and ROLL.
For thermal burns: Cool immediately with cool (not ice-cold) running water for at least 10 to 20 minutes.
Do NOT pop blisters. Do NOT apply ice, butter, oil, or home remedies to burn wounds.
Cover burns loosely with a clean, dry, non-stick cloth or sterile dressing.
FIRE_AND_BURNS.voice_prompt: Evacuate the building immediately. Stay low under the smoke. Once outside in fresh air, cool any burns under running tap water for ten minutes.

ROAD_TRAUMA.title: Road Accident / Polytrauma Protocol
ROAD_TRAUMA.disclaimer: VERIFY AGAINST ATLS (ADVANCED TRAUMA LIFE SUPPORT) BYSTANDER FIRST RESPONDER PROTOCOL. Do not move injured victims unless there is immediate danger of fire or explosion.
steps: Secure the accident scene: Turn on hazard lights or place warning markers so passing vehicles do not cause secondary collisions.
DO NOT MOVE the victim unless there is imminent fire or submerged water risk (suspected spinal cord injury).
If a motorcycle rider is wearing a helmet, DO NOT REMOVE the helmet unless airway is completely blocked.
Check airway and breathing without tilting the neck excessively (use jaw-thrust if trained).
Control any major spurting bleeding with firm direct pressure.
Keep the victim warm with a jacket or blanket while awaiting 108 ambulance.
ROAD_TRAUMA.voice_prompt: Do not move the injured person unless there is immediate fire danger. If they are wearing a helmet, leave it on. Keep them calm and warm until the ambulance arrives.

CHOKING.title: Severe Airway Obstruction / Choking
CHOKING.disclaimer: VERIFY AGAINST RED CROSS HEIMLICH / ABDOMINAL THRUST GUIDELINES. Only intervene if the person cannot cough, speak, or breathe.
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' If they can cough forcefully or speak, encourage them to keep coughing.
If victim cannot breathe, talk, or make sound: Stand behind them slightly to one side.
Deliver 5 sharp back blows between shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
If obstruction remains, deliver 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver): Make a fist, place thumb-side just above navel, grasp with other hand, thrust upward and inward.
Repeat 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object is expelled or patient loses consciousness.
If patient collapses and becomes unresponsive, immediately lower to floor and begin chest compressions (CPR).
CHOKING.voice_prompt: Stand behind the person. Give five sharp blows between the shoulder blades, followed by five quick inward and upward abdominal thrusts just above their navel.
